subject: how to draw a residual variance self-loop with tikz

messages.author: b41ff7fc7cd0f193
messages.subject: how to draw a residual variance self-loop with tikz
parts: LaTeX tikz is good for path diagrams, but does anyone know how to draw a self loop at a node with an arrow head at each end, for example to represent residual variance? (Bit of a side-trip, but useful).

messages.author: b41ff7fc7cd0f193
messages.subject: Re: how to draw a residual variance self-loop with tikz
parts:
One way is to force a curve through a point outside the node, trying to keep continuity through the point: 

\begin{tikzpicture}
\node (A) at (0,0) [circle, draw] {} ;
\draw[latex-latex] (A.north east) to [bend right=60,out=40,in=90] ([xshift=0.5 cm]A.east) to  [bend right=60,out=90,in=140] (A.south east) ;
\end{tikzpicture}

It looks fair but not perfect. Maybe there's an easier way

messages.subject: Re: how to draw a residual variance self-loop with tikz
parts:
I think translating a lavaan model into a tikz diagram cannot work unless for simple diagrams because its almost impossible to generate nice code that can be modified. Probably better is a library of shapes and painful practice with tikz. Here's another go at the variance self-loop looking a bit better.


\documentclass[border=1cm]{standalone}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{shapes.geometric}  % For regular polygon
\usetikzlibrary{calc}

ewcommand{ ikzAngleOfLine}{ ikz@AngleOfLine}
  \def ikz@AngleOfLine(#1)(#2)#3{%
  \pgfmathanglebetweenpoints{%
    \pgfpointanchor{#1}{center}}{%
    \pgfpointanchor{#2}{center}}
  \pgfmathsetmacro{#3}{\pgfmathresult}%
  }

% Add a variance self-loop to a node
%   #1 is the node 
%   #2 is the angle of the centre of the arc from the centre of the node  
ewcommand{\variance}[2] {
  \pgfmathsetmacro{ hetaA}{#2} ;  
  \pgfmathsetmacro{ hetaB}{ hetaA+15} ;
  \pgfmathsetmacro{ hetaC}{ hetaA-15} ;
  \coordinate (D) at (#1. hetaB) ;
  \coordinate (E) at (#1. hetaC) ;
  \coordinate (F) at ([xshift=6mm,rotate around={ hetaA:(#1.center)}]#1.center) ;    % Centre of arc  (xshift should depend on size of node)   
  ikzAngleOfLine(F)(D){\AngleStart}
  ikzAngleOfLine(F)(E){\AngleEnd}    
  \draw[latex-latex] (D) 
    let
      \p1 = ($(D)-(F)$),
      1 = {veclen(\x1,\y1)}      % Radius of arc
    in  
      arc [start angle=\AngleStart, end angle=\AngleEnd-360, radius= 1] ;   % If both angles are in 4th quadrant the arc is short. Then you need to make the start angle be negative, (angle-360).
}

egin{document}

egin{tikzpicture}[
    render/.style = {draw=black!80, fill=black!5, inner sep=0, font=\scriptsize\sffamily fseries},
    lv/.style = {circle, render, minimum size=8mm},         % Latent variable
    ov/.style = {rectangle, render, minimum size=7mm},      % Observed variable
    lm/.style = {regular polygon, regular polygon sides=3, shape border rotate=0, render, minimum height=1cm} % Latent mean
  ]
 
ode (y1)  at (1,0) [ov] {} ;
ode (f1)  at (3,0) [lv] {} ;
ode (lm1) at (5,0) [lm] {} ;

\variance{y1}{90} ;  
\variance{f1}{135} ;
\variance{lm1}{270} ;
 
 \end{tikzpicture}

\end{document}

Here is the syntax I use (assuming the error term is at the bottom of the model and named X):

\draw [<->, thick, >=stealth', bend left=270, looseness=2] (X.south west) to node [swap] {a}  (X.south east);

Best,

Alex
